rationale: Versioned current-ability grades already approved and present in private Wheel authority; historical Oct 3 artifacts remain untouched. No contracts, rosters, development profiles, saved runs or prior Wheel scores rewritten.

grades.reason: Current ceiling: complete passing/creation/rushing profile; one early-2026 turnover game is ordinary noise, not a level change.
Elite processing, arm talent and creation remain established; 2026 start is again high-end, but 2025 prevents a reputation-only 99/100.
Elite passer plus unmatched quarterback rushing stress; current dual-threat level remains just below the absolute ceiling.
2025 MVP and elite full-season passing baseline; early pressure struggles in 2026 are too small a sample for a major downgrade.
Elite placement, processing and pocket passing with a strong 2026 start; no meaningful current gap from Stafford.

Through six 2026 starts: 1,639 yards, 10 TD and 5 INT. Consecutive losses vs Tampa Bay and Green Bay included four interceptions and poor blitz handling; NFL Week 7 QB Index dropped him to No. 19 and documented decision/pressure issues. Preserve above-average veteran ability in 88 rather than overreacting to two games, but the Oct 3 near-elite 92 no longer reflects current execution.
2025 was MVP-caliber, but a 1:6 TD/INT start through three 2026 games is too severe to leave him in the 90 tier. The established ceiling keeps him above the good-starter band.

Strong 2024-25 efficiency and major rushing value remain real, but his current passing level does not support the prior 90 placement. Final cross-position calibration adjusted the grade under the locked range/discrepancy rules.

Owner-approved Oct 8 increase from 89 to 90. Sustained efficient 2025 quarterbacking plus a strong early 2026 showing justify modest placement above Jared Goff 89 and below Dak Prescott 92. This is current functional passing and anticipation, not a small-sample projection bonus.

Sustained elite structured passing in 2024-25 followed by 1,788 yards, 14 TD, 0 INT, and a 112.5 rating through six 2026 starts. The multi-season evidence supports elevating him from very good to high-end in the current NFL grade ladder. Pocket dependence and more limited off-script creation still keep him below the elite upper-90s group; calibrated near Dak Prescott at 92.
Top physical toolkit remains, but 2025 and early-2026 mistakes/volatility do not support grading the idea of Herbert above his actual recent quarterback play.

2025 season produced 4,007 yards and 29 TD; through six 2026 starts he added 1,480 yards, 14 TD, 4 INT and a 106.25 passer rating (8.0 Y/A). Consecutive productive seasons and improved downfield command support a meaningful step above the earlier good-starter 87, with turnover exposure and ceiling consistency short of the elite mid-90s. Current ability 90 aligns with Brock Purdy's tier.

Special rushing/creation ability and a proven high-end rookie season remain real; shortened and less efficient 2025-26 evidence prevents a higher current grade. Final cross-position calibration adjusted the grade under the locked range/discrepancy rules.
Three solid starter seasons through 2025 matter, but a 52.4% completion rate and 83.5 passer rating through three 2026 games pull him back to the solid-starter tier.
2024 showed a high ceiling, while 2025 and the 2026 opening regressed; current thumb availability is an eligibility issue, not an ability penalty.

Seven full 2026 starts, 1,867 passing yards at 7.6 Y/A, 11 TD and just one INT (100.7 passer rating); improved quick game vs blitz and recent sustained passing efficiency. 2024-25 inconsistency prevents elite-tier 92+, and 2023 rookie high-end ability is supported by 2026 return. 88 slots below Purdy 90/Goff 89 and just above Trevor Lawrence 87. Peer-calibrated +6 is supported by material performance reversal, not single-game luck.

After a Super Bowl season, his 2026 line is 1,290 yards and 8 TD/8 INT across six appearances (five full starts), with 62.1% completions. At least one interception in all five full starts through Week 7, with two picks in three of those games and increased sacks/pressure warrant a meaningful current-ability reset, balanced against Week 7's improved efficiency, 2025 performance, and the early hip/line context; this is not a projection of permanent decline.

Seven 2026 Jets games: 1,623 yards, 70.0% completions, 7.8 Y/A, 10 TD and only 2 INT (105.2 rating), reversing the 2025 Raiders season's 19 TD, 17 INT and 84.7 rating. The rebuilt efficiency and ball security warrant above-average starter status. A 21-sack start and recent high-turnover season keep him out of the upper-80s group despite his hot 2026 opening.

Clear development in 2025, especially reducing sacks, plus real creation ability; accuracy/consistency remain uneven enough to stay below the 85 anchor. Final cross-position calibration adjusted the grade under the locked range/discrepancy rules.

Established dual-threat ability remains above replacement-level starter quality; small recent samples are weak, while injury/availability is kept separate from ability. Final cross-position calibration adjusted the grade under the locked range/discrepancy rules. Final discrepancy reconciliation 82→80.

Strong 2025 resurgence is real, but early 2026 regression plus a long prior record of volatility prevents treating that season as a fully established new level. Final cross-position calibration adjusted the grade under the locked range/discrepancy rules.

Seven 2026 starts at Las Vegas have produced 1,877 passing yards, 16 TD, 5 INT, 7.3 yards/attempt and a 97.4 passer rating; this is a substantive rebound from a constrained 2024-25 baseline. Re-established anticipation and accuracy support an above-average current starter, while age, reduced mobility and the prior two-season regression prevent an elite or high-end grade.

Positive 2025 starter sample with meaningful rushing value and a strong two-game 2026 start; still too little NFL evidence for a larger move. Final cross-position calibration adjusted the grade under the locked range/discrepancy rules.

The approved average/solid starter line: competent, stable NFL quarterbacking without high-end creation or sustained difference-making. Final cross-position calibration adjusted the grade under the locked range/discrepancy rules.
Thirteen-game body shows credible starter-level efficiency and enough mobility; ball-security volatility keeps him at the Brissett line.

Six 2026 starts total 1,712 passing yards, 12 TD and 4 INT, with at least two passing TD and at most one interception in four of his first five starts and NFL's Week 7 QB Index placing him seventh among starters entering Week 7. A very poor Week 7 (163 yards, two INT) and 60%-range accuracy prevent an elite regrade; modestly above average current-ability grade acknowledges sustained improvements over his prior baseline.

Owner-approved Oct 8 increase from 79 to 82. Two years of functional NFL starting performance, processing, mobility, and sack avoidance merit the same broadly solid-starter tier as Tyler Shough and Geno Smith (82) and above Jacoby Brissett (80), while inconsistent 2026 deeper accuracy keeps him below Bryce Young (83).

Four encouraging 2026 games now justify a real move upward, but the weak 2022-24 sample and 2025 absence prevent treating the rebound as fully established high-end play. Final cross-position calibration adjusted the grade under the locked range/discrepancy rules. Final discrepancy reconciliation 80→78.

Below-average current starter anchor: still capable of high-level pocket stretches, but 2025 and 2026 efficiency no longer support an above-average grade. Final cross-position calibration adjusted the grade under the locked range/discrepancy rules.

Five 2026 starts through Week 7: 1,157 yards, 9 passing TD against 1 interception on 144 attempts, 8.0 yards/attempt and 109.1 passer rating. His arm talent and decisiveness have materially improved over the 2024-25 baseline. A limited 2026 sample and pressure volatility prevent grading this as a high-end 87+ starter. 83 reflects credible present starter ability, not projected ceiling.

Physical/rushing tools and strong prior spot starts remain useful, but his 2026 starter sample shows accuracy and drive-finishing limitations. Final cross-position calibration adjusted the grade under the locked range/discrepancy rules.

A full 2025 season and early 2026 both show below-average efficiency; enough arm talent and creation keep him above the weakest Wheel options. Final cross-position calibration adjusted the grade under the locked range/discrepancy rules.

No regular-season NFL snaps. Promising flashes were offset by a rough preseason and losing the starting job to Cousins; grade is deliberately provisional and contains no draft-slot projection bonus. Final cross-position calibration adjusted the grade under the locked range/discrepancy rules.
